title: UN OCHA's CERF anticipatory action framework for Philippine typhoons adopted 510's machine-learning impact model as trigger in 2021; no activation on that trigger documented to 2025
summary: OCHA frameworks (2021, 2023, 2025) use 510's XGBoost house-damage model as activation trigger; near-activation Dec 2021 (Rai); the Nov 2025 activation for Uwan ran on the 185 km/h wind trigger.
account: OCHA's Anticipatory Action (AA) Framework for Philippine typhoons was posted on ReliefWeb on 15 September 2021 (date used here). It set up a US$7.5 million CERF pilot for about 270,500 people in Regions 5 and 8 with FAO, IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF and WFP. It has a two-stage trigger. The readiness trigger is PAGASA and 510 forecasts of a category 4 or stronger cyclone. The activation trigger, within 72 hours of landfall, is the IFRC/Netherlands Red Cross 510 probabilistic typhoon impact prediction model's predicted number of totally damaged houses. The framework says that model partially uses a machine learning model relating wind speed to housing damage. 510's 2024 NHESS paper (vendor-authored) states the XGBoost model served in 2021 as the trigger model for the UN OCHA AA pilot. OCHA's After Action Review of 31 March 2022 records that Typhoon Rai (Odette) in December 2021 rapidly intensified and did not meet the activation criteria. There was a near activation with staff pre-deployed. The 2023 revision retained the 510 model. The framework endorsed on 19 October 2025 covers US$6 million CERF and about 955,507 people in Regions 5, 8 and 13. OCHA and its Centre for Humanitarian Data compute predicted totally damaged buildings with the 510 model every 6–12 hours. It adds an observational trigger for super typhoons of 185 km/h or more reported by PAGASA. OCHA's June 2025 report says the readiness trigger was met for Super Typhoon Pepito (Man-yi) in its November 2024 to April 2025 reporting period. Activation thresholds were not reached and CERF AA resources were reallocated to the response. On 6 November 2025 CERF AA was activated for Super Typhoon Fung-Wong (Uwan) after the observational wind-speed threshold was triggered. OCHA reports nearly US$6 million released and WFP alone reaching 42,100 families. No read document records an activation produced by the 510 model's output.
purpose: Forecast the number of totally damaged houses from typhoon track, wind and rainfall forecasts so that CERF-funded early actions can be triggered before landfall. The benefit claimed (AI-triggered anticipatory payouts) is that purpose, but no activation on the model's output is documented.
system: 510 probabilistic typhoon impact model (XGBoost) predicting totally damaged houses, used as the CERF anticipatory action activation trigger
model_version: probabilistic version using ECMWF ensemble tracks (revamped from deterministic, 2021)
developer: 510, an initiative of the Netherlands Red Cross, with IFRC
deployer: UN OCHA Philippines with the CERF AA Core Group (FAO, IOM, UNFPA, UNICEF, WFP); impact estimates generated by 510 (2021 framework) and by OCHA with its Centre for Humanitarian Data (2025 framework)
domain: Humanitarian anticipatory action / typhoon impact forecasting
taxonomy_note: Loose fit; the model supplies impact estimates that decide whether anticipatory funds are released, and no activation attributable to it is documented.

ratings.reason: General benefit: no activation attributable to the model's output is documented, so no individual-level outcome can be assigned to the AI.
General benefit: OCHA adopted the model as its trigger and computes estimates each cycle. The only documented activation (6 November 2025) was triggered by the observational wind-speed threshold.
General benefit: pre-landfall assistance in November 2025 (WFP reports 42,100 families) is documented, but not attributed to the AI model by any source on file.

ai_role.statement: OCHA's 2021, 2023 and 2025 frameworks name the IFRC/510 impact model as the activation-trigger model. The 2021 framework describes it as partially a machine learning model. This is documented by the deployer, not only the maker. The model's forecasts were monitored during the December 2021 near activation (Typhoon Rai) without meeting criteria. The 2024 readiness phase for Pepito ended with CERF AA resources reallocated to response. OCHA's flash update attributes the 6 November 2025 activation for Uwan to the observational threshold (forecast peak 195 km/h against the 185 km/h trigger). It does not state that the 510 model's estimates reached the activation matrix. The AI's contribution to any payout is therefore not established. The maker's NHESS paper is the only source describing the algorithm (XGBoost).

produced_by: A pre-arranged CERF allocation with agency action plans ready before the typhoon season
ECMWF ensemble track, wind and rainfall forecasts fed to the 510 impact model every 6–12 hours
Historical house-damage data linking hazard, vulnerability and exposure to train the model
A threshold matrix of predicted totally damaged houses per region with a 1-in-3.5-year return period (2025)
must_hold: Forecast lead time of at least 72 hours; rapid intensification (Rai 2021) shortened lead time below the trigger window
Model impact estimates reaching the regional threshold matrix, which no read activation record documents
Agency delivery capacity (financial service providers, data-sharing agreements) in the 72 hours before landfall

echoes.setting: Typhoon Rai (Odette), December 2021: forecasts monitored, activation criteria not met, staff pre-deployed (near activation)

Super Typhoon Pepito (Man-yi), within OCHA's November 2024 to April 2025 reporting period: readiness trigger met, activation thresholds not reached, CERF AA resources reallocated to emergency response
Super Typhoon Fung-Wong (Uwan): CERF AA activated on the observational 185 km/h threshold; nearly US$6 million released; WFP reports 42,100 families reached; AI model's role not stated

headline: OCHA uses 510's model as CERF trigger; no activation documented

later.note: The framework stayed in force and CERF anticipatory action was activated for Super Typhoon Fung-Wong (Uwan) on 6 November 2025 with nearly US$6 million, but on the observational 185 km/h wind threshold rather than on the 510 model's output.
later.quote: The CERF Anticipatory Action (AA) was activated on 06 November after the observational threshold for Tropical Cyclone Fung-won (Uwan) was triggered. Nearly US$6 million has been allocated to five United Nations agencies to implement AA and early response efforts.
